principles: Each facet answers one question. A concept has exactly one home: a subject is a topic, what the statement does is its statement type, money is a finance fact.
Only statement_type is required. Every other list may be empty; empty means 'nothing extracted', never 'the country has none'.
Select a value only when the record's own evidence supports it. A word match is not evidence.
Closed facets accept only listed IDs. Facets marked closed_with_other also accept {id: 'other', source_term: '...'}; recurring source terms are reviewed for promotion to a listed value.
Code derives everything that can be derived (domains, response stage, rollups). The model is never asked to produce a value that code can compute.
A reviewer may set review_status on a record, relation or claim. That is the only edit ever made to a model output; anything else is a re-run with a new version.

record_facets.label: Statement type
record_facets.question: What does this statement assert?
record_facets.rule: One value per coherent proposition. Split independently actionable measures, and split promises from reports of delivery. response_stage is looked up from this value by code; it is never asked of the model.

values.label: Context or finding
values.definition: A condition, trend, risk, need, barrier or observed hazard impact, with no undertaking. Includes 'no warning system exists'.

values.label: Projection or scenario
values.definition: An estimated future condition or effect based on modelling or assumptions. Scenario names and horizons go in facts.

values.label: Proposal or recommendation
values.definition: An action suggested or recommended without established adoption by the responsible government.

values.label: Priority or goal
values.definition: An area or goal stated as important by the reporting party, without a concrete undertaking. An actionable priority is a commitment.

values.label: Commitment or target
values.definition: An attributable undertaking to achieve a goal or target, quantitative or qualitative, conditional or not, without a specified measure for how.

values.label: Planned action
values.definition: A specific measure, instrument, programme or project describing what will be done. A target paired with a defined measure is a planned action.

values.label: Implementation underway
values.definition: The source reports allocated or mobilised resources, procurement, construction or an operating programme. A finance need or estimate is not resourcing.

values.label: Output delivered
values.definition: The source reports a completed, checkable output: a law or plan adopted, a system installed, a facility built. Delivery does not prove the intended outcome.

values.label: Result reported
values.definition: A reported change in an outcome linked to a response (losses fell, coverage rose). Not a response stage; it sets the claim's outcome signal.

values.label: Unclear
values.definition: The evidence does not support a reliable type. Explain why in notes.

record_facets.label: Policy purpose
record_facets.question: What policy purpose does the source state or clearly establish?
record_facets.rule: Leave empty when no purpose is established. A NAP location alone does not establish adaptation. 'Flood mitigation' is disaster risk reduction, not mitigation.

values.label: Adaptation
values.definition: Adjustment to actual or expected climate effects and their consequences.

values.label: Mitigation
values.definition: Reducing greenhouse-gas emissions or enhancing carbon sinks.

values.label: Disaster risk reduction
values.definition: Preventing new disaster risk, reducing existing risk or managing residual risk.

record_facets.label: Hazard
record_facets.question: Which potentially damaging process is discussed?
record_facets.rule: Use only when the hazard is substantively discussed. A hazard is not exposure, vulnerability or a policy purpose. Earthquakes and tsunamis are never climate evidence.

values.label: Flood
values.definition: Riverine, flash, pluvial or snowmelt inundation of normally dry land. Keep the flood type in the statement.

values.label: Heavy precipitation
values.definition: Intense rain or snowfall discussed as a hazard in its own right.

values.label: Drought
values.definition: A sustained precipitation or water deficit.

values.label: Water scarcity
values.definition: Insufficient usable water relative to demand; distinguish from drought when the source does.

values.label: Extreme heat
values.definition: Heatwaves and unusually high temperatures.

values.label: Extreme cold
values.definition: Cold waves, frost and severe winters.

values.label: Storm or high wind
values.definition: Damaging storms, hail and high winds.

values.label: Dust or sand storm
values.definition: Wind-blown dust or sand events.

values.label: Wildfire
values.definition: Uncontrolled vegetation fire.

values.label: Landslide or mudflow
values.definition: Downslope movement of soil, rock or debris, including mudflows (sel).

values.label: Avalanche
values.definition: Rapid downslope movement of snow or ice.

values.label: Glacial lake outburst flood
values.definition: Sudden release of water from a glacial or moraine-dammed lake.

values.label: Glacier, snow or permafrost loss
values.definition: Retreat of glaciers, reduced snowpack or permafrost thaw.

values.label: Desertification or land degradation
values.definition: Loss of land productivity, including soil erosion and salinisation.

values.label: Sea-level rise
values.definition: Rising mean sea level, including in inland seas when the source frames it so.

values.label: Coastal hazard
values.definition: Storm surge, coastal flooding and coastal erosion.

values.label: Disease or biological hazard
values.definition: Epidemics, vectors, pests and other biological threats.

values.label: Earthquake
values.definition: Seismic ground shaking and its secondary effects.

values.label: Tsunami
values.definition: Waves generated by displacement of water.

values.label: Technological or industrial
values.definition: Industrial, chemical, radiological, dam-failure or tailings accidents.

values.label: Compound or cascading
values.definition: Hazards explicitly discussed as concurrent or triggering each other.

record_facets.label: Risk component
record_facets.question: Which part of risk does the statement describe?
record_facets.rule: Use only when the statement explicitly concerns that component. A hazard mention does not establish exposure or vulnerability.

values.label: Hazard
values.definition: The damaging event, process or trend itself.

values.label: Exposure
values.definition: People, livelihoods, assets or systems located where hazards occur.

values.label: Vulnerability
values.definition: Conditions that make exposed people or systems more susceptible to harm.

values.label: Capacity
values.definition: Resources, skills and institutions available to manage risk, or their absence.

values.label: Impact
values.definition: Losses, damage or consequences that occurred or are projected.

values.label: Residual risk
values.definition: Risk remaining after measures.

values.label: Systemic or cascading risk
values.definition: Risk spreading through linked systems.

record_facets.label: Risk function
record_facets.question: What does the action do about risk?
record_facets.rule: Applies to actions in any sector. Topics say what the action is about; this says what it does about risk. Leave empty for generic 'resilience' wording.

values.label: Risk understanding
values.definition: Assessing hazards, exposure, vulnerability or risk, or producing risk information.

values.label: Prevention and reduction
values.definition: Avoiding new risk or reducing existing exposure or vulnerability.

values.label: Warning and preparedness
values.definition: Warning capability, contingency plans, exercises and readiness to act.

values.label: Anticipatory action
values.definition: Action triggered by a forecast before an event. General readiness is not enough.

values.label: Emergency response
values.definition: Protecting people and meeting urgent needs during or right after an event.

values.label: Recovery and reconstruction
values.definition: Restoring livelihoods, infrastructure and services, including rebuilding more safely.

values.label: Coping and continuity
values.definition: Keeping essential functions running during disruption through buffers or backups.

values.label: Systemic transformation
values.definition: Fundamental change of systems or development pathways. Routine improvement is not enough.

record_facets.label: Affected or target group
record_facets.question: Which people does the statement explicitly address?
record_facets.rule: A mention does not establish a benefit. Never infer a group from a sector (an agriculture topic does not imply farmers). Named organisations are stakeholders, not groups.

record_facets.label: Cross-cutting theme
record_facets.question: Which cross-cutting issue does the statement treat substantively?
record_facets.rule: Only for substantive treatment. Themes that already exist as topics (finance, livelihoods, just transition, data, local knowledge) are not repeated here.

values.label: Gender equality
values.definition: Gender roles, gaps, participation or outcomes are analysed or addressed.

values.label: Social inclusion
values.definition: Inclusion of youth, older people, persons with disabilities or other marginalised groups is addressed.

values.label: Poverty and inequality
values.definition: Poverty or distributional effects are analysed or addressed.

values.label: Participation
values.definition: Consultation, stakeholder engagement or participatory processes.

values.label: Capacity building
values.definition: Institutional, technical or human capacity development.

values.label: Technology transfer
values.definition: Technology development, access or transfer.

values.label: Transboundary cooperation
values.definition: Cooperation across national borders.

values.label: Nature-based solutions
values.definition: Using ecosystems or natural processes, when that role is evidenced.

record_facets.label: Policy instrument
record_facets.question: What mechanism is used or proposed?
record_facets.rule: Classify the mechanism, not the sector. A policy document does not by itself establish legal force.

record_facets.label: Geographic scope
record_facets.question: At what geographic level does the statement apply?
record_facets.rule: Record only an explicit or unambiguous scope. Named places go in places. EU-level or regional statements are never reassigned to the reporting country.

linked_fields.label: Stakeholder role
linked_fields.question: What does the named organisation do in relation to this statement?
linked_fields.rule: Keep the source name. A ministry mention does not establish responsibility; use unspecified.

linked_fields.label: Linked detail kind
linked_fields.question: What non-numeric supporting information is linked to the record?

linked_fields.label: Missing-value reason
linked_fields.rule: Only for blanks that change interpretation, such as a target with no baseline. Unreadable pages belong in coverage, not here.

linked_fields.label: Page disposition
linked_fields.rule: Every page in scope gets exactly one disposition. not_found statements are only valid for extracted or background pages.

linked_fields.label: Review status
linked_fields.question: Has a person checked this record against the PDF?
linked_fields.rule: Absent or null means not reviewed. A rejected record stays in the file for the audit trail but is excluded from stage 2 and from every view. A wrong label is never corrected in place: reject the record, fix the prompt or the vocabulary, and re-run.

fact_fields.rule: Every number becomes a fact with its own period, condition, scope and evidence. Never turn an observation, projection or finance need into a target. Unknown is null, never zero. Do not compare facts until metric, unit, baseline, denominator, period, scope, scenario and condition match.
